en.t: It was not long before I went to Tokyo to serve drinks.

units.source_text: 那阵子手头钱不富裕，自己买不起日记本，

en.t: At that time money was tight, and I could not afford to buy myself a diary.

units.source_text: 只好花两三分钱买来一本杂记本，

en.t: I had no choice but to buy a notebook for two or three sen.
Then I ruled fine lines on it with a ruler.

units.source_text: 也许是铅笔削得很尖，划出来的线整齐美观极了。

en.t: Perhaps because the pencil had been sharpened to a very fine point, the lines came out wonderfully neat and beautiful.

units.source_text: 所以从本子上角到下角，密密麻麻地写满了小字。

en.t: So I filled the notebook from the top corner to the bottom corner with tiny, densely packed writing.

units.source_text: 等到自己买得起日记本，反而不行了，用起来很浪费。

en.t: Once I could afford to buy my own diary, though, it was no good; I used it wastefully.

units.source_text: 就说练字吧，本来常在旧报纸上写，现在就直接在成卷的信纸上写罗。”

en.t: Take handwriting practice, for example: I used to write on old newspapers, but now I write directly on rolls of letter paper.
